observations: Piray & Daw (Nature Communications 2024) directly separate volatility from stochasticity: both raise observation variance, but volatility raises autocorrelation while stochasticity lowers it; participants and their hierarchical Bayesian model use this temporal structure to attribute uncertainty.

Pulcu & Browning (eLife 2025) report that humans adapt to estimated noise but imprecise uncertainty representations can misattribute stochasticity as volatility, matching the predecessor audit's stable-overdispersion false-change failure mode.

Wilson, Nassar & Gold (Neural Computation 2010) remains the hazard-learning reference; the predecessor audit already showed most benefit came from a Bayesian regime posterior rather than adaptive hazard itself.

Godin & Thivierge PLOS Computational Biology 2026 still exposes S1 Code.zip at DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014719.s002. Read-only recovery was retried through the current public article route, but file-level ZIP contents were not obtained; no connector mutation or probe side effect was used.

bounded_audit.scope: Synthetic bounded causal control continuing the prior SPLiT-derived latent-cause/dormant-memory branch. This is not an exact reproduction of SPLiT, Piray-Daw, Pulcu-Browning, Wilson-Nassar-Gold, PAST, or GROUSE.

design.stochasticity_model: A separate latent high-stochasticity state uses a mean-preserving symmetric mixture of geometric duration distributions with component means 0.45m and 1.55m. This explicitly models observation stochasticity rather than weakening all surprise with a generic outlier term.
design.semantic_cue: P(S)=0.9 for true S and 0.1 for true C; cue-loss windows use 0.5.

controllers.hand_accumulator: Decayed clipped alternative-vs-current duration likelihood score, decay=0.96, threshold=6 for 3 consecutive events.
controllers.fixed_hazard_bayes: Two duration-regime states, symmetric hazard 0.01, clean emission model.
controllers.adaptive_hazard_bayes: Same two-state filter with discounted Beta hazard posterior initialized at mean 0.01.
controllers.dual_latent: Four-state Bayesian filter over duration regime R x stochasticity state Z. R flip hazard=0.01; Z flip hazard=0.001. Semantic-cause likelihood is marginalized using the noisy cue.

design.decision_rule: Regime change is counted after posterior probability of the new regime exceeds 0.97 for 2 consecutive events.
design.heldout_semantic_eval: 128 paired seeds per change scenario; stable-overdispersion false-activation stress expanded to 512 paired seeds. Paired bootstrap 95% intervals are over seed-level controller differences.
design.fast_memory_probe: A disjoint 48-seed calibration selected P(temporary-silence)>0.95 with restore blend=0.6 for a fast normalized one-dimensional circular subspace-tracker proxy (eta=0.25). Held-out memory tests use 96 seeds for overdispersed-swap and cue-loss-swap, and 64 seeds / 500 events for repeated-switch stress. This proxy is PAST/GROUSE-like in role and timescale but is not source-exact PAST/GROUSE.

stable_overdispersion.interpretation: Explicitly representing stochasticity removes most Bayesian false change alarms under matched overdispersion, but the hand accumulator remains the most conservative false-alarm baseline.

stable_overdispersion_noise_state_diagno.interpretation: The separate noise state is identifiable in this matched model but adapts slowly; its long warm-up is a likely source of residual false alarms.

overdispersed_swap.interpretation: The main cost of explicitly modeling stochasticity appears when a true regime change occurs while stochasticity is already high: some coherent change evidence is temporarily explained as noise.

calibration.selected_rule: restore pre-event dormant direction only when dual-latent semantic posterior P(temporary-silence)>0.95; blend=0.6
calibration.selection_note: Chosen on disjoint seeds for strongest post-silence/overall benefit among tested thresholds while observing zero persistent-change admissions in calibration.

memory_results.interpretation: With matched stochasticity inference and a strong semantic cue, the calibrated fast restore improves post-silence recovery and does not produce resolved post-switch harm in these held-out streams. The negative post-change deltas reflect carry-over from better pre-change tracking; the controller made no direct restore admissions on persistent-change events.

mechanistic_interpretation.positive: Separating a persistent duration-regime latent variable from an observation-stochasticity latent variable resolves the predecessor audit's noise-to-volatility confusion under the matched generative family. It cuts stable-overdispersion Bayesian false activations by 3.71 percentage points while retaining 15-27 event speedups over the conservative hand accumulator on abrupt, cue-loss, gradual and repeated changes. Fast dormant-memory restore remains beneficial under the guarded semantic posterior in the tested streams.
mechanistic_interpretation.negative_boundary: The benefit is not free. The dual filter produces 0.78% stable-overdispersion false activations versus 0% for the hand accumulator, and a true change under already-high stochasticity is detected about 5.52 events later than the single-latent fixed Bayesian filter. More importantly, the high-stochasticity emission family is correctly specified here; this is an oracle-family advantage until robustness to misspecified, correlated, skewed and nonstationary noise is tested.
mechanistic_interpretation.neuroscience_connection: Piray-Daw provides a direct computational-neuroscience precedent for representing volatility and stochasticity separately rather than mapping all surprise to environmental change; their empirical signature is temporal covariance/autocorrelation. Pulcu-Browning supplies the complementary failure mode: coarse uncertainty representations misattribute noise as volatility. The current audit supports that design principle in this narrow synthetic duration setting, not the specific human model or neural implementation.

limits: The high-stochasticity duration likelihood exactly matches the simulator's mean-preserving mixture; robustness under likelihood misspecification is unknown.
Semantic cues are relatively strong outside explicit cue-loss windows.
The dual filter is a four-state HMM, not Piray-Daw's hierarchical particle filter and not full volatility/stochasticity diffusion inference.
The memory tracker is a transparent fast normalized subspace proxy, not source-exact PAST/GROUSE or SPLiT.
The audit does not recover or execute SPLiT S1 Code.zip.
All positive and negative conclusions are restricted to the stated synthetic duration and circular tracking regimes.
bounded_audit.exact_next_action: Continue read-only SPLiT S1 Code.zip recovery without mutation. Stress the dual-latent controller under stochasticity-model misspecification: correlated bursts, skewed/heavy-tailed duration noise, drifting noise scale and changes in stochasticity itself. Add a Piray-Daw-inspired covariance/autocorrelation attribution channel or hierarchical variance/covariance learner and compare it against the current oracle-family four-state filter, regime-only Bayes, and a flexible nonparametric/noise-mixture control. Require stable-noise false alarms to stay below the single-latent Bayesian filters without adding more than the current ~1 event delay on clean abrupt/gradual/repeated changes or the current ~5.5 event penalty during high-noise true changes. Then replace the circular memory proxy with a genuine O(Nk) PAST/GROUSE-style subspace update, weaken/delay semantic cues, recalibrate on disjoint seeds, and retain dormant-memory restore only if post-silence recovery remains resolved while post-switch interference remains unresolved. Preserve label-symmetry abstention, exact tested scope, CLEAN isolation and a nonempty frontier.
